headline: Ericsson beat profit and sales forecasts but warned that the AI boom is raising its component costs, so it is raising equipment prices.
score_reason: Company results with a clear cost warning from the new chief executive; one outlet read, so REPORTED.
importance_line: Phone and network customers could eventually pay more, as operators and Ericsson share the cost of AI-driven component prices, but the timing depends on contracts and BigGo's account of the call is not independently confirmed.
summary: BigGo Finance reports that Swedish telecom equipment maker Ericsson's third-quarter revenue rose 6% to SEK 59.5 billion, beating forecasts, and its shares jumped as much as 11%, the biggest daily gain since January. New chief executive Per Narvinger said AI demand is raising component costs, that Ericsson has raised prices in new bids, and that mobile operators may pass higher costs on to consumers, with long-term contracts possibly weighing on margins through 2027.
notes: BigGo Finance's own write-up of the results and call; the original results release and call transcript were not read.
